classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the two elevations in one triangle, convert the nearer elevation to an interior angle, select the sine rule for BT, then use a right-triangle ratio to obtain the height.

content.prompt: The angle of elevation of the top $T$ of a tower from a point $A$ is $45^\circ$. Point $B$ lies 25 metres closer to the tower along the horizontal line from $A$ to its base. From $B$, the angle of elevation of $T$ is $78^\circ$. Find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the length of $BT$ correct to 2 decimal places

answer.worked:
In triangle $ABT$, the interior angle at $B$ is supplementary to the angle of elevation.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABT&=180^\circ-78^\circ\\\angle ABT&=102^\circ\\\angle ATB&=180^\circ-45^\circ-102^\circ\\\angle ATB&=33^\circ\\\frac{BT}{\sin45^\circ}&=\frac{25}{\sin33^\circ}\\BT&=\frac{25\sin45^\circ}{\sin33^\circ}\\BT&\approx32.46\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the height of the tower correct to 2 decimal places

answer.worked:
Let the tower's height be $h$. Use the unrounded expression for $BT$ from part (a).
$$\begin{align*}\sin78^\circ&=\frac{h}{BT}\\h&=BT\sin78^\circ\\h&=\frac{25\sin45^\circ\sin78^\circ}{\sin33^\circ}\\h&\approx31.75\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
